question.problem:
Suppose we wish to find a zero of the function $f(x,y)$ in the region $[0.5,1]\times [1,1.5]⊆{R}^{2},$ where $$ f(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}3{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}-4 \\ x{y}^{3}-2\end{aligned}]. $$ Fill in the blanks in the matrix equation below that defines the first iteration of the Newton-Raphson process starting at the point $[1,\,1]^{T}.$
$[$ {{field-1}} {{field-2}} $]({x}_{1}-{x}_{0})\,=[$ {{field-3}} $].$
$1$ $3$ $1$
question.worked_solution:
The Newton-Raphson method of finding the zeros of a multivariable function $f:{R}^{n}\to {R}^{n}$ is

$$
{x}_{n+1}={x}_{n}-[{J}_{f}({x}_{n})]^{-1}f({x}_{n}),
$$

where ${J}_{f}({x}_{n})$ is the Jacobian of $f$ evaluated at ${x}_{n}.$

Equivalently, at each iteration, the above equation can be re-written as

$$
{J}_{f}({x}_{n})({x}_{n+1}-{x}_{n})=-f({x}_{n}).
$$

In our case, the Jacobian is

$$
\begin{aligned}{J}_{f}(x) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂x}(3{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}-4) & \frac{∂}{∂y}(3{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}-4) \\ \frac{∂}{∂x}(x{y}^{3}-2) & \frac{∂}{∂y}(x{y}^{3}-2)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}6x & 2y \\ {y}^{3} & 3x{y}^{2}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our Newton-Raphson system of equations is

$$
{[\begin{aligned}6x & 2y \\ {y}^{3} & 3x{y}^{2}\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{n}}({x}_{n+1}-{x}_{n})=-{[\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}-4 \\ x{y}^{3}-2\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{n}}.
$$

Starting with ${x}_{0}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{[\begin{aligned}6x & 2y \\ {y}^{3} & 3x{y}^{2}\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{0}}({x}_{1}-{x}_{0}) & =-{[\begin{aligned}3{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}-4 \\ x{y}^{3}-1\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{0}} \\ [\begin{aligned}6(1) & 2(1) \\ {1}^{3} & 3(1)(1)^{2}\end{aligned}]({x}_{1}-{x}_{0}) & =-[\begin{aligned}3(1)^{2}+(1)^{2}-4 \\ (1)(1)^{3}-2\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}6 & 2 \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}]({x}_{1}-{x}_{0}) & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
